text:
sara: Heads-up — apiserver 5xx spike in us-west1 started ~5m ago, coinciding with a big GPU onboarding churn. Not full outage but elevated errors and client retries.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] apiserver 5xx surge detected (us-west1) 30 error rate x7 over baseline.

sara: logs: 
``
E0815 13:05:12 apiserver.go:300] proxy error: dial tcp 10.1.50.7:6443: connect: connection reset by peer
E0815 13:05:12 apiserver.go:315] watch queue length: 4120
```

liam: digging infra metrics  - NAT ephemeral ports at 97%, conntrack spiking on kube-proxies.

nick: autoscaler launched ~180 preemptible GPU nodes at 12:58 — parallel attaches + image pulls look like the trigger.

jade: etcd commit latency nudged up ~150ms during the spike; leader stable but followers retransmitted.

sara: short-term plan: 1) throttle autoscaler attach concurrency (liam), 2) enable port-preserving SNAT / spin secondary NAT (liam/jade), 3) route control-plane egress to spare NAT if needed (nick).

liam: I'll roll a small canary to set max_parallel_attach=4 and attach_backoff=30s. Also enabling port-preserve now.

finance-bot: [INFO] Temporary extra NAT cost estimate = $210/day.

sara: alerts to add: nat_ephemeral_usage > 90% for 1m, apiserver_watch_backlog > 1000 for 2m, etcd_commit_latency > 120ms for 1m.

jade: INFRA-8401 created to track NAT sizing, autoscaler throttling, and a follow-up to reduce monitoring sidecar sockets during onboarding.

sara: agreed on medium-term: reserve small dedicated GPU pool for critical lanes and move control-plane egress off shared customer NATs. will reconvene after canary. Thanks all.
